questions.question: When slowing down, you should ____ to warn other drivers

options.text: Use a turn signal
Sound your horn
Tap your brakes

questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brakes before slowing down. This makes your brake lights flash and warns drivers behind you.

questions.question: How much water must be present for a vehicle to hydroplane?

options.text: Usually several inches
A good amount, such as a large puddle
A small amount

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose grip and slide on water. Only a small amount of water is needed for this to occur.

questions.question: After arriving at a destination, a driver should:

options.text: Rest.
Remind passengers to take their belongings with them when they exit.
Only make announcements after passengers have begun to exit the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remind passengers to take their belongings with them when they exit.
questions.explanation: When arriving at a stop, remind passengers to take their belongings before exiting. Make this announcement before the bus fully stops.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Change a tire.
Explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.
Estimate the weight of a load on a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do a complete inspection. Explain to the examiner what you are checking and why.

questions.question: A cargo van is:

options.text: Usually the same height with or without a load.
Usually taller with a heavy load than with a light load.
Usually shorter with a heavy load than with a light load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually shorter with a heavy load than with a light load.
questions.explanation: A heavy load makes a vehicle sit lower. A vehicle is taller when lightly loaded than when fully loaded. If your vehicle fits under an overpass when full, it may not fit when empty.

questions.question: If you are unfamiliar with the area where you must back up, you should:

options.text: Get out of your vehicle and walk around the area to become more familiar with it.
Not use both side mirrors because it can be distracting.
Wait for someone else to back up in the area so you can see how they do it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of your vehicle and walk around the area to become more familiar with it.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, get out and look at your path. Check the clearance on all sides and overhead.

questions.question: The two indicators that determine when you should upshift are:

options.text: Engine speed and road speed.
Other trucks and driving conditions.
Timing and road position.

questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift up: engine speed (rpm) and road speed (mph). Check your manual for your vehicle's rpm range. Shift up when you reach the top of that range. Also watch your speedometer and shift up as speeds increase.

questions.question: Emergency roof hatches on a bus:

options.text: Must be closed before the bus is driven.
Can be opened to allow for air movement during a drive.
Must be removed before the bus is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be opened to allow for air movement during a drive.
questions.explanation: Some emergency roof hatches can be locked open to let in fresh air while driving. However, this should not be done regularly.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should:

options.text: Always pump the brakes several times before holding down the brake pedal.
Brake normally.
Press down the brake pedal as hard as possible every time you slow or stop.

questions.explanation: Brake the same way in vehicles with ABS and without ABS. ABS works automatically to prevent wheel lockup when you brake.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter a cab due to:

options.text: A defective exhaust system.
Using the wrong type of fuel.
A lack of oil in the engine.

questions.explanation: A faulty exhaust system is a serious safety problem. It can allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: During a CDL vehicle inspection test, what will you be asked to do?

options.text: Check the engine oil level.
Replace a tire.
Remove the alternator belt.

questions.explanation: The vehicle inspection test includes checking the oil level. You must show that the oil is at a safe level.

questions.question: What does a standee line on a bus do?

options.text: Shows where riders cannot stand.
Helps passengers get on and off the bus.
Is part of the air conditioning system.

questions.explanation: On a bus with standing room, passengers cannot stand in front of the driver's seat. The bus must have a line or marking on the floor showing this no-standing area. This is called a standee line.

questions.question: When should a driver sign a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: After every trip
After defects are repaired
After each fueling

questions.explanation: Sign a vehicle inspection report only if defects were found and have been repaired or certified as not needing repair.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: With both hands.
With one hand to keep the other hand free.
With one hand at a time, switching between hands.

questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: When inspecting your vehicle, which of these do you NOT need to check?

options.text: Too much air pressure in your tires.
Too little air pressure in your tires.
The brand name is the same on all tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brand name is the same on all tires.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check that tire air pressure is not too high or too low. Tire brand names do not need to match.

questions.question: How can you warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down?

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Tap the brakes lightly a few times before braking.
Turn on one set of turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap the brakes lightly a few times before braking.
questions.explanation: Before slowing down, lightly tap your brake pedal a few times. This flashes your brake lights and warns drivers behind you that you plan to slow down.

questions.question: Which person should NOT concern motorists as a distraction?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger in their vehicle
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
A construction worker on the side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Watch out for people who are not paying attention to the road. Drivers and pedestrians talking to someone may be distracted and not notice traffic. Workers near the road may focus on their work and not watch for traffic.

questions.question: What should you know about people working on a disabled vehicle?

options.text: They are probably watching the roadway.
They may be focused on repairs and not notice traffic.
They do not have to follow traffic laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may be focused on repairs and not notice traffic.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people working on a disabled vehicle on the roadside. They may focus on the repair and not pay attention to nearby traffic.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT cause hydraulic brake failure?

options.text: Loss of hydraulic pressure
Brake fade from long hills
Downshifting

questions.explanation: Hydraulic brake failure usually happens in two ways: loss of hydraulic pressure or brake fade from overuse on long hills. Downshifting does not cause hydraulic brake failure.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: Before starting a trip
While driving
When stopped at a traffic signal

questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you start each trip. If you have a trailer, it should be straight when you adjust the mirrors.
